newsitem.title: USA: No recall plans for Kennedy-Smith - White House.
newsitem.headline: No recall plans for Kennedy-Smith - White House.

text.p: The United States has no plans to recall U.S. Ambassador to Ireland Jean Kennedy Smith or to make major changes in its Ireland policy, a White House spokesman said on Monday.

The spokesman was responding to a question about British and Irish newspaper reports suggesting that Smith was expected to leave her post and the United States might throw its weight behind Anglo-Irish efforts to isolate Sinn Fein, the Irish Republican Army's (IRA) political wing.

"There are certainly no plans to recall Ambassador Smith and the United States maintains its intense interest, which starts at the president, in doing whatever we can in helping the people of Ireland to find peace," said White House spokesman David Johnson.
"The suggestions that we are considering sharp changes in our policy are absolutely false," he added.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns also said Smith had the president's full support.

"She retains full and unequivocal support of the president and Secretary of State (Madeleine) Albright," Burns told reporters. "There has been no decision by the administraiton to recall her because of any perceived dissatisfaction with how the peace process has gone."
British and Irish news reports suggested that Clinton wanted to replace Kennedy with someone who is seen to be less sympathetic to the Irish Republican cause.

Clinton has been closely involved in promoting the peace process and his 1995 decision to allow Sinn Fein to raise funds in the United States angered the British but helped prod the nationalists toward talks.
He visited Belfast in November 1995 and appointed former U.S. Sen. George Mitchell to head an international commission meant to oversee moves toward peace.
But the peace moves were dealt a big setback a year ago when the IRA ended a ceasefire with a bomb blast at London's Canary Wharf complex.

The IRA, which seeks to end British rule of the province, has bombed security targets in Northern Ireland several times every week this year to back its demand that its political wing, Sinn Fein, be invited to peace talks.
